title: It’s easy and the food is good
review: I suffer from severe depression and if something is too hard, I can’t do it. Cooking is one of those things - eating healthy is almost impossible for me. Finding easy recipes, figuring calorie intake, and compiling a shopping list is overly daunting. Then you add another layer of finding food that you would actually eat on top of having easy to find ingredients and healthy eating becomes overwhelming. Then add that you don’t want to cook everyday vs making a ton of food for the week that you get tired of after day 3 and healthy eating is out of reach. This app takes away all of that work. It calculates your caloric intake, compiles a weekly list of recipes, you can arrange or swap out recipes based on your schedule or ingredients, and it compiles a shopping list. You can filter out food dislikes and food allergies. The recipes are easy. They are delicious. It’s worth the price for the time savings. My only suggestion is linking this with food tracking apps - my fitness pal, noom, etc.

title: This app changed my meal planning for my family of 6!!
review: There should be a service where you tell someone your macros and they give you meal ideas! I wish I had found this sooner because my meal prep has been overwhelming. I don’t enjoy thinking of new recipes that are healthy and that my family will eat, I don’t enjoy making grocery lists, and I definitely don’t enjoy figuring out weights based off of what my macros should be. This app does it all for you! I can even add my own personal recipe macros. They have delicious and clean recipe ideas and my family has enjoyed all of them. One complaint: hopefully one day it’ll give you the option to swap out an ingredient.

title: They have thought of EVERYTHING to help a person be successful at meal planning!!
review: The app creates a menu for you & if you don’t like what it chooses, you can swap out individual meals. You can also add your own recipes. It also has a shopping list organized by store sections. The only downside: it measures by ounces instead of teaspoons, tablespoons, & cups, so I have to look up the conversions every time bc I don’t want to weigh things.

title: Still My #1 Meal Prep App (With One Frustration)
review: My biggest struggle in the gym was my nutrition. As someone with ADHD, I struggle with meal planning that meets my fitness goals. MealPrepPro has made that so much easier. With one tap I get a full week of meals planned, a grocery list automatically created, and recipes that actually taste good. The one thing keeping this from being a 5-star app is the Custom Macros feature. I follow a structured training plan with specific macro targets, but the app won’t let me enter those exact numbers. I get an “invalid macro values” error. If Custom Macros allowed truly free-form macro targets within a chosen calorie range, this would be an easy 5-star app for me.

title: Thorough Tracking, but Limited Customization
review: I do like this app and appreciate it for its user interface and thorough meal planning help. However, a few tweaks would make it worth it. The first is allowing temporary food additions to your day. If you want to add a quick snack, you have to create it as a permanent recipe. My second suggestion is being able to add an ingredient list to your manually added recipes, allowing them to generate a shopping list. Lastly, the app’s recipes are completely unchangeable - if you sub full fat cream cheese for low fat, you cannot tell the app and have it adjust calories. I won’t be rolling my free trial into a subscription because of these issues.

title: Great app, suggestions
review: I work 12-13 hour shifts and don’t have time to cook. One issue is that it doesn’t give exact portion sizes. It would be nice to have portion weights. I wish there was a swap for sides or grains/veggies. The recipes are a bit bland, and I do tweak them with seasonings. Another thing, the weekly prep is kind of flawed: I picked 4 days in a row but the recipe cuts off at 2 because it hits the weekend.

title: Wow!!!
review: Diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes. I had gone through a couple of other apps, but none of them were helpful. But this app is so on point. I have a clear calendar of what to eat and when, a platform that allows me to click one button to show I have eaten the meal, and stats that are meaningful and easy to review. Most importantly, the food is absolutely scrumptious.

title: I LOVE this app! Keep the vegan recipes coming!
review: I have been a vegetarian for 15 years and dabbled in veganism. After 5 months of exercise I was not seeing my weight go down. I realized that while my diet was healthy, I was missing the mark. I started looking into macro counting but the thought of managing my finicky vegetarian/vegan diet on top of macros seemed overwhelming. While researching, I found MealPrepPro and decided to give it a try. In four weeks I am down 7.5 lbs while eating good food and not going hungry. The recipes are delicious and quick, the grocery lists are invaluable and the ability to switch out recipes incredibly simple.

title: Great food, but Portions are way too big!
review: I love the shopping list and being able to mark off ingredients. The biggest problem is the portions. Based on my weight and height the app suggests I eat up to 1800 calories which isn’t unreasonable but for even the 3 day meals I make enough that at a glance I feel like I could eat for a whole week. I would rate five stars because the app is very nice and easy to use and the recipes are much better than I would make on my own, but the portions upset the balance.

title: Implement more instructional videos please!
review: This app would be great if it had more instructional videos showing the process of the cooking. It’s kinda hard for me to follow the written steps, it gets confusing at some points. Most of the recipes recommended to me for my diet don’t even have an instructional video for me to follow and it’s pretty frustrating.
